25 A source of sound waves is travelling as shown.
In which situation would the stationary observer detect the largest decrease in the observed
frequency?
A
B
observer
source
observer
source
5 m s–1
10 m s–1
C
D
observer
source
observer

5 m s–1
10 m s–1

hints: Look at each arrow: left means the source on the right is moving toward the observer, right means it is moving away from the observer.
Recall for Doppler effect that moving toward gives $f_o > f_s$ and moving away gives $f_o < f_s$, with observed wavelength $\lambda_o = (v \pm v_s)/f_s$.
Compare only the two receding cases C at $5 \text{m s}^{-1}$ and D at $10 \text{m s}^{-1}$ and decide which speed stretches $\lambda_o$ more.
walkthrough: Identify the geometry: observer is on the left, source is on the right. An arrow to the left is motion toward the observer, an arrow to the right is motion away.

State the Doppler rule: approaching source crowds wavefronts together so $\lambda_o$ is smaller and $f_o = v/\lambda_o$ is higher; receding source spreads wavefronts so $\lambda_o$ is larger and $f_o$ is lower.
Therefore A and B with $5 \text{m s}^{-1}$ and $10 \text{m s}^{-1}$ toward the observer both give an increase in frequency and cannot be the largest decrease.
For a receding source, $\lambda_o = (v + v_s)/f_s$, so larger source speed $v_s$ gives larger $\lambda_o$ and smaller $f_o = v/\lambda_o$.
Compare C with $v_s = 5 \text{m s}^{-1}$ away and D with $v_s = 10 \text{m s}^{-1}$ away: D produces the larger $\lambda_o$ and the lower $f_o$.
This is option D as the largest decrease in observed frequency.

A.explanation: Source moves at $5 \text{m s}^{-1}$ toward the observer, so wavefronts bunch up and observed frequency increases, not decreases.

B.explanation: Source moves at $10 \text{m s}^{-1}$ toward the observer, giving an increased observed frequency, not a decrease.

C.explanation: Source moves away at $5 \text{m s}^{-1}$, so frequency decreases, but the stretch of wavelength is smaller than for $10 \text{m s}^{-1}$ away.

D.explanation: Source moves away at $10 \text{m s}^{-1}$, giving the most stretched observed wavelength and so the largest drop in observed frequency.
